The primary bug_semantics misnames repeat_len - INT32_MIN as signed integer underflow. Because repeat_len is nonnegative, the mathematical result is greater than INT_MAX: the C++ operation is signed overflow/undefined behavior; buffer underflow is the reported downstream memory symptom.

corrected_fields.bug_semantics: llama.cpp's DRY sampler accepts caller-supplied dry_allowed_length as signed int32 without a lower bound. HTTP /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions can supply INT32_MIN; json_value and llama_sampler_init_dry preserve it, the early-return and repeat eligibility comparisons become ineffective, and repeat_len - dry_allowed_length produces a mathematical value above INT_MAX, causing signed integer overflow and undefined behavior. The advisory reports the resulting heap buffer underflow/OOB read as SIGSEGV denial of service or corrupted sampling probabilities. The same unbounded integer is also accepted by --dry-allowed-length.
